paragraphs.source_en: From Keichō 8 (1603) onward, the capital enjoyed unprecedented prosperity, and its people lived in peace and contentment. By the time of the Hōkoku Festival in the ninth year, that prosperity seemed to have taken firm root. By the summer of the tenth year, the world seemed to have entered an age of perfect peace, and the wars felt like something from another lifetime.

units.source_en: From Keichō 8 (1603) onward, the capital enjoyed unprecedented prosperity, and its people lived in peace and contentment.

units.source_en: By the time of the Hōkoku Festival in the ninth year, that prosperity seemed to have taken firm root.

units.source_en: By the summer of the tenth year, the world seemed to have entered an age of perfect peace, and the wars felt like something from another lifetime.

paragraphs.source_zh: 自庆长八年（一六○三）始，京城出现了前所未有的繁荣，百姓亦安居乐业。九年举行丰国祭时，此种繁荣已有落地生根之势。至十年夏，人间似乎已成太平盛世，战乱恍若隔世。

paragraphs.source_en: Tokugawa Hidetada's entry into the capital briefly stirred ripples amid its bustle, yet in the end it unexpectedly dispelled the people's anxieties altogether. When word first spread that Hidetada was coming to the capital with an army of 160,000 to assume the office of shogun, people throughout Kyoto and Osaka prepared to flee. Only through the energetic persuasion and exertions of the shoshidai Itakura Katsushige, Chaya Shirōjirō Kiyotsugu, Hon'ami Kōetsu, Suminokura Yoichi, and others was widespread disorder averted. Before long, a magnificent ceremony was held to mark the completion of Kōdai-ji.

paragraphs.source_zh: 德川秀忠入京，曾在一片繁华中激起些许微澜，不意最后反而彻底消除了百姓的不安。最初听说秀忠携十六万大军赴京就任将军之位，京坂各地百姓纷纷作好了逃难准备。后来，经过所司代板仓胜重及茶屋四郎次郎清次、本阿弥光悦和角仓与市等人积极游说奔走，才未发生大骚乱。不久，便举行了盛大的高台寺落成礼。

paragraphs.source_en: Toyotomi Hideyori's proposed visit to the capital came to nothing because of opposition from the lords of the Kinai region and Lady Yodo, and some discerning people quietly worried about what this might portend. Yet afterward, it was said, Tokugawa Ieyasu not only declined to pursue the matter but instead sent his sixth son, Tadateru, to Osaka Castle in Hidetada's stead to inquire after Hideyori's health. Only after Hidetada had successfully presided over Kōdai-ji's completion ceremony and departed to take up his duties in Edo did the world finally breathe freely, convinced that the course of the realm was now settled.

paragraphs.source_en: The temper of the people in and around the capital was utterly transformed. One sign that people's hearts had truly settled was the crowding of spectators, even at midsummer, around the variety-show booths erected in the precincts of Kitano Tenmangū and near the banks of the Shijō River. Among them were not only residents of the capital but envoys who had come from every province to pay their respects, as well as travelers eager to experience the peace and prosperity for themselves.
